briefs.headline: Barcola hat trick carries Liverpool past LASK 6-3
briefs.summary: Bradley Barcola's first Liverpool goals came in the 24th, 37th and 66th minutes Wednesday in Linz; Ronald Araujo, Jeremie Frimpong and Lewis Koumas also scored. Liverpool have won both league-phase matches.

briefs.headline: Mendez, Zaroury and Habroune lift Crew past Charlotte 3-1
briefs.summary: Idan Toklomati put Charlotte ahead in the 17th minute Wednesday; Brais Mendez equalized in the 28th and Anass Zaroury and Taha Habroune scored in the 63rd and 65th. Columbus visits FC Cincinnati Sunday at 5 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati fall 3-2 to New England at TQL Stadium
briefs.summary: Tom Barlow scored in the 13th minute Wednesday, but Dor Turgeman scored twice and Joshua Wynder once before Kevin Denkey replied in the 67th. "At this stage, we need to defend in a better way," Pat Noonan said.

briefs.headline: Pirates' Lowe and Triolo named Gold Glove finalists
briefs.summary: Rawlings named Brandon Lowe a finalist at second base and Jared Triolo, the 2024 NL utility winner, at utility Wednesday; winners are announced Nov. 1 on ESPN. Lowe had plus-15 outs above average this year.

briefs.headline: Spurs beat Suns 123-103 as Fox makes preseason debut
briefs.summary: Victor Wembanyama had 19 points and four blocks Wednesday as Mitch Johnson used De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle together for the first time. San Antonio has one preseason win in four games; Sacramento visits Friday at 8 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Rodriguez says WVU will keep using two-tailback sets
briefs.summary: West Virginia leads the nation with 1,773 rushing yards and is fourth at 295.5 a game; Cam Cook's 793 yards rank third, per WV MetroNews Wednesday. Cincinnati visits at noon ET Saturday on TNT for homecoming.

briefs.headline: Brewers beat Dodgers 6-2, lead the NLCS three games to none
briefs.summary: Jake Bauers' two-run homer and Garrett Mitchell's solo shot off Blake Snell in the seventh erased a one-run deficit Wednesday in Los Angeles; Ohtani, batting sixth, singled and walked. Game 4 is Thursday.

briefs.headline: MLB moves ALCS Game 3 in Cleveland up to 1 p.m. ET for rain
briefs.summary: The Rays-Guardians game at Progressive Field, originally 6 p.m., airs on TBS with Gavin Williams facing Griffin Jax; the series is tied at a game apiece. NLCS Game 4 also moved up, to 8 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Astros drop Espada a day after clearing a Mariners interview
briefs.summary: Houston said Wednesday it will not renew Joe Espada's contract, which expires this month, despite two AL West titles in three seasons; the White Sox swept the Astros in the wild-card round.

briefs.headline: Tuch scores twice as Capitals hold off Canadiens 5-4
briefs.summary: Alex Tuch's second goal, with 2:55 left Wednesday in Washington, stood up after Nick Suzuki answered 76 seconds later; Josh Anderson scored twice for Montreal. Washington has won four of seven.

briefs.headline: Stars beat Avalanche 3-2 in a four-round shootout
briefs.summary: Roope Hintz converted the deciding attempt Wednesday in Denver after Jason Robertson and Nazem Kadri traded shootout goals; Arttu Hyry put Dallas ahead in the third, Brock Nelson tied it for Colorado.

briefs.headline: Rams' Jackson has punch suspension cut to one game on appeal
briefs.summary: Hearing officer Derrick Brooks halved the two-game ban Wednesday; Jackson misses Sunday at Arizona, with David Quessenberry at left tackle. Bradley Chubb said he taunted Jackson about chip blocks.

briefs.headline: Seahawks and Broncos meet Thursday night short of starters
briefs.summary: Seattle ruled out LB Drake Thomas and RB Zach Charbonnet; Denver is without Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga, both ankle injuries. Each has won three of five; 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video.

briefs.headline: Four arrested in February nightclub shooting of 49ers' White
briefs.summary: San Francisco police said Wednesday the arrests came over the past week with help from Atlanta, Stockton, Irvine and Los Angeles; Keion White was shot in the ankle Feb. 9 at a Super Bowl party.

briefs.headline: UCLA's Iamaleava out against Wisconsin with a knee injury
briefs.summary: Wednesday's Big Ten injury report rules him out; coach Bob Chesney called the job "decently fluid" between Ty Dieffenbach and Madden Iamaleava. UCLA is unbeaten in five and No. 12 in the AP poll.

briefs.headline: Michigan judge clears two fifth-year transfers to play
briefs.summary: Judge Julia Owdziej granted a restraining order for TE Alex Bauman and DB Jeremiah Earby against the NCAA's 2022-class rule; Ohio's Supreme Court will rule on DeWine's order, briefs due Monday.

briefs.headline: Oregon's Moore out a second straight game against Nebraska
briefs.summary: Dante Moore remains out after a Sept. 26 concussion; Dan Lanning said Wednesday the start is open among Dylan Raiola, who struggled at UCLA, Brock Thomas and freshman Akili Smith Jr.

briefs.headline: Medvedev beats Tsitsipas as Shanghai quarterfinals begin
briefs.summary: Daniil Medvedev won in straight sets Wednesday and plays Tommy Paul on Friday; Alejandro Davidovich Fokina reached the semifinals Thursday when Arthur Gea retired. Zverev-de Minaur is at 6 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Antonelli could clinch the F1 title in Austin on Oct. 24
briefs.summary: He leads Mercedes teammate George Russell by 102 points with 150 left; ESPN reported Thursday that F1 still plans to finish in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, with Imola as a fallback. Austin is Oct. 23 to 25.

briefs.headline: Tobizaru, 34, braces for a first drop to juryo since 2020
briefs.summary: Likely to fall to juryo (the second division) after four wins and 11 losses in September with a sore elbow, he took two days off and spars daily on the jungyo (regional tour): "My heart has not rotted."

briefs.headline: Hakkaku named honorary citizen of his Hokkaido hometown
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association chairman, the former yokozuna (grand champion) Hokutoumi, received Hiroo's sixth-ever honor Oct. 11 after the town dropped its residency rule; about 250 attended.

briefs.headline: Autumn tour reaches Nagahama with Kyushu 24 days out
briefs.summary: The jungyo (regional tour) is in Nagahama today and Kyoto Friday, ending Oct. 25 in Ube; the banzuke (rankings) is out Oct. 26 and the Kyushu basho (tournament) opens Nov. 8 in Fukuoka, 24 days out.

prime.item: Day 1. Proclamation SF-1-2026, signed Oct. 2 by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler and re-opened this morning at 5:50 a.m., makes the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise today, Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation. The recreational limit it sets is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, seven days a week, by hand and hand-operated implements only; it is unlawful to possess oysters under three inches shell length, to take oysters between sunset and sunrise, or to take them from the oyster sanctuaries listed in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:49 a.m. and still dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, reads oysters as season closed, unlawful to possess; the proclamation is the later document and the one that opens the season. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:49 a.m. and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, under federal red drum management; the division's flounder proclamation FF-27-2026, which the page links, cites Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124 requiring recreational anglers to report red drum, spotted seatrout, flounder, striped bass and weakfish harvest to the division. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries, and a Coastal Recreational Fishing License is a separate license from the inland one. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 14 days old, has red drum as the main inshore target around Topsail.

prime.dates: Open; 14- to 20-inch slot, one over 26 inches

The reference file records the harvest reopening July 1 after the February cold-stun closure. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 14 days old, has the trout not yet cooperating, a few on early topwater.

prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists Spanish mackerel at 12 inches fork length and 15 per day, king mackerel at 24 inches fork length and three per day, and bluefish with no minimum size and five per day, all under federal management plans. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 14 days old, has Spanish and bluefish plentiful from the surf and piers and kings to 32 pounds at Jolly Roger Pier.

NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists black drum at a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, sheepshead at 14 inches total length, five per day, neither under federal regulation, and spot with no minimum size and 50 per day under federal spot management. The reference calendar lists October as the peak of the spot run; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 14 days old, has black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs, spot in the evening bottom-fishing catch at Surf City Pier and sheepshead in the Seaview Pier bottom catch.

sections.label: On the Water
sections.note: All four waters reported from the locked fishing.json, generated_at 2026-10-15T05:43:54-04:00, errors list empty; the file was not re-run by this desk and every figure is printed as it stands there. At 25.4 on a normal pool, with the gauge in its ordinary band and the Kanawha's new water not yet in it, the river fishes the structure itself: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam and along the riprap where the current breaks, a half-ounce blade bait or a jigging spoon on the lock wall's deep edge for the sauger, crawfish-colored jigs in the rock for the smallmouth, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and flatheads after dark, a 17 percent crescent setting early and leaving the water dark. waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 11:44 PM (Wed) and 12:16 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Fifth day past the new moon: the fetcher's file carries the moon as a waxing crescent, 17 percent lit and 4.0 days old, and the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, which answered at 5:48 a.m., puts the new moon at 15:50 UT Saturday, Oct. 10, the first quarter at 16:12 UT Sunday, Oct. 18, the full moon at 04:12 UT Oct. 26 and the last quarter at 20:28 UT Nov. 1, so the spring tides are still on but easing toward Sunday's neap: the surf's morning swing has come down from 5.3 feet Monday, 5.0 Tuesday and 4.6 Wednesday to 4.1 today. NWS Wilmington had no product for Coastal Pender at 5:48 a.m., no rip current statement, no high surf advisory, no coastal flood advisory, the fourth quiet beach morning in a row. The sound at Hampstead is at the bottom of its ebb at press time, a 0.8-foot low at 5:49 a.m. off the 3.3-foot high of 11:44 p.m. Wednesday, which is last night's tide and is printed with its weekday tag so nobody reads it as tonight's; it then fills 3.3 feet to a 4.1-foot high at 12:16 p.m., drains 2.9 feet to a 1.2-foot low at 6:41 p.m., so the last two hours of the ebb, about 4:30 to 6:41 p.m., land in the late afternoon in daylight, and fills after dark toward a high that falls after midnight and belongs to Friday's table. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: low 4:24 a.m. at 0.9, high 11:05 a.m. at 5.0, low 5:38 p.m. at 1.1, high 11:23 p.m. at 3.5, a 4.1- and 3.9-foot swing against Wednesday's 4.6 and 4.4. Today's lags from the two tables are 71 minutes on the midday high and 85 and 63 minutes on the lows, with last night's sound high 65 minutes behind Wednesday's surf high; the morning low again lags longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat hour's offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 76.3 degrees at 5:36 a.m., up 0.7 from Wednesday's 75.6 and the warmest reading of the week. What is running is 14 days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:49 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings starting to show at the piers, trolled spoons working off the beach, and inshore red drum as the main target, scattered through the ICW, the creeks and the inlets, with no word on trout yet; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, a few trout on early topwater, glass minnows thick off the beach and the kings still in 50 to 60 feet; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout in the first hour of light on Spook Jrs. and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds on shrimp at the bridges and oyster reefs; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or Gulp under popping corks, flounder as bycatch, false albacore due on the nearshore structure; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small metal and epoxy jigs; South End has the bigger Spanish in 45 to 50 feet over hard bottom under diving birds and kings in the 8- to 12-mile range. The piers: Jolly Roger reports bait everywhere, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem: the sound is slack low at 5:49 a.m., dead water at first light, and the first moving water is the morning flood from about 6:30 a.m., mud minnows and shrimp the forage on the oyster bars and grass edges as they cover, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars on the early flood, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead as the bars go under. The 12:16 p.m. high puts 4.1 feet of water over the grass and up the dock pilings, which is where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about 10:15 a.m. to 12:16 p.m., then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the ebb, roughly 4:30 to 6:41 p.m., a daylight ebb 43 minutes later than Wednesday's with no beach product over it: finger mullet are the forage the file records and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, and a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low. On the evening flood after 6:41 p.m. the dock lights are the trout spot once the 17 percent crescent sets, though with Beaufort up to 76.3 the cool-down the report says the trout are waiting on has not come. Oysters opened at sunrise today under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. The surf side, with no advisory on it and 5.0 feet of water at the pier on the 11:05 a.m. high, is Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs for the Spanish and bluefish on the morning flood and cut bait on the bottom for the slot reds in the evening, the pattern every pier in the report gives. Slack at 5:49 a.m., 12:16 p.m. and 6:41 p.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only.
